problem.explanation: A self join gives the employees table two roles: e is the employee and m is the manager. LEFT JOIN preserves top-level employees, and COALESCE supplies the label. A common mistake is an inner join, which removes people without managers. Recursive CTEs are needed only for full reporting chains.
hints: The employee and manager are rows in the same table.
Use a self LEFT JOIN and COALESCE the manager name.
problem.reference_solution: SELECT e.name AS employee, COALESCE(m.name, 'No Manager') AS manager FROM employees e LEFT JOIN employees m ON e.manager_id = m.id ORDER BY e.name
problem.statement_markdown: Return every employee and their manager name. Show 'No Manager' when manager_id is NULL or unmatched. Sort by employee name.
problem.title: Employee and manager names
